analysis: Examined the ProviderLoop.swift head excerpts (lines 544-1116) and the LaunchAgent.swift patch plus base text. The substantive change in ProviderLoop.swift (lines 451-454, not shown as a head_text unit) adds `releasedAdmissions` and `coldLoadReleasesWorkFIFO` state for releasing the work FIFO during model-load waits. The visible excerpts contain only unchanged declarations and init code. In LaunchAgent.swift, five new env keys are added to `inferencePassthroughEnvKeys`: PromptTokenCachePolicy (environmentKey, capacityEnvironmentKey, verifyEnvironmentKey), ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.environmentKey and WorkFIFOPolicy.coldLoadReleaseEnvironmentKey. These keys are copied from the installing shell into the launchd plist `EnvironmentVariables` through `passthroughEnvironment` (head ~322-343), and only for non-empty values. The list is a fixed allowlist, so no arbitrary env injection was added. The shell operator is the same local principal who controls the plist, so there is no privilege boundary crossing. Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix-cache and TTFT oracle, SEC-035). The new `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE` introduces a prompt-token reuse cache described as 'scoped' and on by default. It is distinct from the SSD KV prefix cache. Its implementation is not in the supplied evidence: the scoping (per-account cacheSalt), the at-rest posture, memory residency, and whether it affects T-028/T-041 cross-tenant timing or retention. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. The cold-load FIFO release changes request ordering and admission state (`releasedAdmissions`). Whether it interacts with cancellation, draining, or per-request key and plaintext cleanup (T-008, T-010, A-001) is also not visible. Next review should examine PromptTokenCachePolicy and its storage, scoping and TTL, plus ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift and the cleanup paths for ReleasedAdmission. No concrete regression is established from the supplied lines.
